title: Finding where a downstream check neutralizes the apparent vulnerability
scenario: The fee calculation genuinely overflows into an absurd value, but the value is clamped to a maximum before it is ever used, so the miscomputation never reaches a security-sensitive operation.
exercises: a real defect whose value is never consumed produces no impact
the technical anomaly is preserved while the impact claim is refuted

mutations.name: a neutralized defect cannot be adjudicated as a supported impact
mutations.expect_error: adjudication.impact is SUPPORTED but prosecutor.elements.impact.basis is not demonstrated

mutations.name: the blocked consumption step must remain blocked in the path
mutations.expect_error: adjudication.attack_path is SUPPORTED but step 4 is BLOCKED

challenged_finding.claimed_impact: Fee overflow lets an attacker set an arbitrary protocol fee

prosecutor.strongest_claim: An unchecked multiplication in the fee path produces an arbitrary fee for attacker-chosen inputs.

attacker_capability.statement: Any address can call quote() with arbitrary size.

execution_path.statement: The unchecked block wraps and returns a fee far above the intended bound.

violated_property.statement: The computed fee stays within the configured maximum.

impact.statement: The inflated fee is charged to counterparties.

defender.strongest_counterargument: _clampFee() bounds the value to MAX_FEE_BPS before any caller consumes it, so the overflow never reaches a charge.

challenges.statement: Every consumer of quote() routes through _clampFee(), which bounds the result to MAX_FEE_BPS.

evidence.ref: grep -n quote( contracts/: all call sites pass through _clampFee

challenges.statement: No stored state retains the raw value for later use.
quote() is reachable, but only the clamped result is observable.

challenge_matrix.finding: quote() is permissionless and the unchecked block executes as described.
No precondition beyond a large size argument.
The raw value is never stored; it exists only in memory.
Every call site clamps the result, so no consumer sees the overflowed value.

assumptions.statement: The multiplication overflows for attacker-chosen inputs.
Some consumer uses the unclamped value.

evidence.ref: grep -n quote( contracts/: all call sites clamp

assumptions.statement: The clamp bound is itself attacker controlled.

attack_path.transition: Attacker calls quote() with a size that overflows the multiplication.
The unchecked block returns a wrapped fee value.
The value passes through _clampFee() before any use.
A counterparty is charged the inflated fee.

counterexamples.reason: The overflowed value is clamped to MAX_FEE_BPS at every call site before it is charged, so the miscomputation is never consumed in a security-sensitive operation.

evidence.ref: grep -n quote( contracts/: 4 call sites, all clamped

decisive_facts.fact: The unchecked multiplication does overflow for attacker-chosen inputs.
All four call sites clamp the value before charging.

severity_challenge.demonstrated_impact: An overflowing intermediate value that is clamped before use
severity_challenge.attacker_requirements: None beyond gas, but the outcome is bounded by the clamp.
severity_challenge.policy_alignment: The program requires a demonstrated impact; a clamped intermediate value does not reach any impact tier.
unproven_dependencies: A consumer that reads the unclamped value

adjudication.strongest_supporting_evidence: The unchecked multiplication genuinely overflows, as the executed test shows.
adjudication.strongest_opposing_evidence: Every consumer clamps the result before use, so the overflow is never observed downstream.
adjudication.rationale: The miscomputation is real and worth reporting as a code-quality defect, but the impact chain terminates at the clamp; the impact and severity claims are refuted while the anomaly itself stands.
